intro: The same TEPEX-style plan at 10° N, 95° W in the Gulf of Tehuantepec, flown 15 times on two dates: the Petrel glider surveys 2 km north at 5–100 m depth, the Tern boat stays over it (1 km acoustic modem), and the Gnat quad relays 30 m above the boat for 20 minutes, then flies home (300 m radio). Wind from WRF, currents from HYCOM, waves from WAVEWATCH III. The vehicles are the stand-in examples, so the point here is what the simulator does with real weather, not the verdict for the real platforms.
rows:
2023-03-07, 17 UTC
one WRF snapshot, held constant

UMARGINAL (80 % of runs succeed, 90 % interval 59–92 %). Glider GO, arrives in 76 min. Boat GO, within 11 m of the glider. Both range requirements GO (peaks 222 m and 55 m apart). The quad lands with a median 22 % battery and goes under its 15 % reserve or flat in 3 of 15 runs: shorten its stint or carry more battery.

NNO-GO. February is gap-wind season here. The seas exceed the boat's design-category C limit (2.0 m significant wave height) in every run, and the quad's median battery at landing drops to 18 %. The glider, underneath it all, is still GO in 77 min, and both links hold.
Either date: the glider deployed 8 km from a boat holding station, 2 km modem
NNO-GO on the link: never in range, about 9.4 km apart. The glider also can't cover its 2 km leg in the 1 h given.
